items.title: A map of invertible sheaves induces a norm map on their norms, and vanishing of the map is detected at a point exactly when the norm map vanishes there
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma produces from any O_X-linear map of invertible sheaves a norm map on the norms, and states that such a map is zero at a point over y exactly when its norm map is zero at y (statement lines 3695-3715). The counted proof is short, 19 lines, but it contains a checkable construction: after trivializing the two invertible sheaves over a suitable open covering, the given map becomes multiplication by local functions f_j and the induced map is defined as multiplication by their norms, with the construction of the cited norm sheaves supplying the cocycle identity that makes the local definitions glue; the final equivalence is then exactly condition (2) of the definition of a norm map of degree d (proof lines 3718-3733). It is H2 under the lane rule that a short proof containing a checkable construction or replacement is still H2, and the closing sentence in which the author leaves routine details to the reader covers the cocycle bookkeeping only, not any clause of the statement.
